claims.text: The proposed scope is CrFeCoNiX high-entropy alloys with X equal to Si, Mn, or Al, in single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution states.
The relevant exposure boundary is an oxidative or corrosive atmosphere above 900 °C.
High-temperature oxidative or corrosive exposure causes formation of a stable, coherent protective oxide layer on CrFeCoNiX alloys.
Configurational entropy provides the thermodynamic stability governing formation and persistence of the protective oxide layer.
Low atomic diffusion governs formation and persistence of the protective oxide layer.
The protective oxide layer persists during continued high-temperature exposure.
The persistent protective layer prevents oxide cracking or spallation.
Uncoated or unalloyed CrFeCoNiX material is the proposed baseline.
Oxide thickness, oxide composition, and corrosion rate can be measured to test the hypothesis.
Failure of the oxide layer to remain stable or prevent cracking or spallation would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The baseline is described as 'unalloyed CrFeCoNiX,' but CrFeCoNiX is intrinsically an alloy; no specific element removal or alternative baseline composition is defined.
The intervention is environmental exposure rather than application of a coating, so an 'uncoated' baseline does not differ from the stated test material in the manipulated variable.
